# SB-1016 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Hazard description

An unplanned arc flash event occurred adjacent to the induction power cabinet serving the Heat Treat heat treat furnace identified as EQ-P2-L4-HT02. The event originated during a quench cycle and resulted in localized burning of insulation on control wiring, damage to the power cabinet door, and a brief loss of control communication to the furnace. Root-cause analysis indicates that the arc flash was initiated by a rapid energy transfer in the cabinet coincident with a delayed quench sequence. The energy release pathway included cabinet internal metallic surfaces and exposed terminal blocks not isolated by the existing barrier arrangement.

This hazard poses risk of severe thermal injury to personnel performing energized troubleshooting or routine access, risk of collateral equipment damage that can interrupt heat treat processing on line P2-L4, and risk of ignition of nearby combustibles if not addressed. The incident demonstrates that the current protection and procedural controls were insufficient to prevent an arc flash during abnormal sequencing of the quench system.

Background: EQ-P2-L4-HT02 operates with an electrically actuated quench process. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds. The control logic permits a maximum delay before the quench actuation completes; delays beyond expected behavior can create conditions for arcing if power paths remain live and contacts are exposed. Existing risk assessments did not fully account for an arc initiation occurring during extended quench delay.

## Affected equipment

- Induction power cabinet for EQ-P2-L4-HT02, including high-current bus runs, contactor assemblies, and control terminal plates.  
- Adjacent control panels and wiring harnesses located within the same cabinet footprint on line P2-L4.  
- Personnel performing cabinet access, troubleshooting, or any activity that requires the cabinet to be energized or open while power is present.

Reference related maintenance and operating documents for detailed procedures: MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-04.

## Required controls

The following controls are required immediately and must be implemented before any energized access to the induction power cabinet:

- Administrative control: All energized troubleshooting or access to the induction power cabinet must be authorized through the site energy control coordination process specified in SOP-P2-L4-02. Authorization must document that arc flash hazards have been reviewed and that electrical isolation is impractical only after documented justification consistent with MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.

- Work sequencing: When work requires that the cabinet remain energized, the affected work must be planned to eliminate exposure of personnel to live metal parts. Use insulated tooling and extend the use of insulating barriers inside the cabinet as described in SOP-P2-L4-04. If live work is unavoidable, ensure an approved energized work permit is in place that includes task-specific controls and verification requirements.

- Control logic verification: Before returning the cabinet to service after any maintenance or after a quench event, verify that the quench control timing matches documented values and interlocks. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds. Any deviation from the expected timing must be corrected and documented prior to restart.

- Physical barriers and labeling: Install additional insulating barriers to isolate terminal blocks and bus connections exposed during routine access. Apply durable arc-hazard warning labels to the cabinet exterior and to all serviceable panels. Labels and barriers must comply with the signage and guarding guidance in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.

- PPE and training: Personnel entering the arc boundary around the cabinet must wear PPE consistent with the risk assessment defined in SOP-P2-L4-02 and must be trained in energized work safety. Training records required by SOP-P2-L4-04 must be current and available at the worksite.

Rationale: Administrative authorizations and energized work permits reduce the likelihood that personnel will perform unplanned live work. Physical barriers reduce the probability of flashover between live components and accessible metal. Verifying quench timing addresses the specific mechanism identified in the incident and prevents the sequence condition that contributed to the arc flash. PPE and training mitigate consequence should an arc event occur despite controls.

Examples of acceptable controls: using insulated probe extensions to verify control voltages without removing panels; confirming control relay drop-out via remote indicators before door entry; applying temporary insulating shields over known exposure points during diagnostic work as allowed by SOP-P2-L4-04.

## Records to keep

Maintain the following records in the document control system entry for SB-1016 and attach them to the work order when controls are applied:

- Energized work permit or authorization described in SOP-P2-L4-02.  
- Control logic verification checklist signed by responsible engineer. The checklist must reference EQ-P2-L4-HT02 and include a confirmation that the quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds.  
- Installation verification of insulating barriers and labels with photos.  
- Training verification records required by SOP-P2-L4-04 for personnel involved in cabinet access.  
- Incident report and root-cause analysis documentation per MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 where applicable.

These records must be retained according to the retention rules in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 and be made available for review by plant safety leadership and maintenance auditing.

## Effective date

Effective date: Upon issuance of this bulletin (Rev A). Implement required controls immediately and include verification records with the next maintenance activity involving EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Review the controls during the next scheduled safety audit and update risk assessments in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 as needed.

For questions or clarifications contact the P2 safety lead or the heat treat line engineer assigned to P2-L4. Follow SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-04 for procedural detail and MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 for maintenance specific requirements.
